summary:
A July 2026 legal risk assessment map places Rhode Island in its most protective tier for gender-identity nondiscrimination. The map states that its top tier can no longer be considered most protective nationwide, so the ranking describes the state's own law rather than conditions a visitor will meet at every point of the journey.

Gender identity or expression has been protected against discrimination since 2001 in employment, credit, housing and public accommodations under R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 28-5-3, 28-5-7, 34-37-4, 34-37-4.3 and 11-24-2. Sexual orientation has been protected in the same fields since 1995. A bill signed in June 2023 added explicit bans on discrimination in patient care, nursing and related healthcare, and the exemption that had permitted discrimination in owner-occupied housing with three or fewer occupants was repealed with effect from 1 January 2023.

Hate-crime law under R.I. Gen. Laws § 42-28-46 provides penalty enhancements for crimes motivated by a victim's actual or perceived gender identity or expression. The gay and trans panic defence was repealed in June 2018 by votes of 68-2 in the House and 27-0 in the Senate, signed by Governor Gina Raimondo a month later and effective immediately.

State-issued identity documents are comparatively open. Since 23 October 2014 a birth certificate gender change has required a Birth Certificate Request Form and an affidavit from a physician, certified nurse practitioner or physician's assistant confirming transgender status, replacing an earlier surgery requirement. The Division of Motor Vehicles issues a corrected driver's licence on a Gender Designation Form signed by the applicant. An X option on driver's licences and birth certificates was announced in August 2019 and available from July 2020. A June 2018 law requires transgender people to be correctly recorded on death certificates. Passports and visas are issued under national rules and are not covered by this record.

Single-occupancy toilets may legally be designated gender-neutral from 1 January 2022 under a bill signed in July 2021.

Rhode Island is covered by shield laws or executive orders from the 2023 and 2024 batches, which make protections enforceable against out-of-state action.

Conversion therapy on minors and state funding for such practices were prohibited by a law signed on 19 July 2017 by Governor Raimondo and effective immediately, after House votes of 69-0 and 62-0 and a Senate vote of 29-0.

In March 2025 the Rhode Island Interscholastic League updated its transgender athletes policy. Transgender athletes remain able to compete, but member schools are responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable state and federal law when determining gender-based eligibility, replacing a policy that allowed participation consistent with gender identity.
tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 map's protective tier is an assessment of state law rather than a guarantee of treatment on the ground, and the map itself states that the top tier can no longer be considered most protective nationwide.

The March 2025 change to interscholastic eligibility defers to member schools' reading of national law, so the practical reach of the state's participation policy depends on decisions taken school by school.

The 2023 and 2024 shield provisions are enforceable against out-of-state action, which matters to a visitor or a clinician whose home jurisdiction restricts or criminalises the care in question.

The X option on state driver's licences and birth certificates does not extend to passports or visas, which are issued under national rules.
localsOnly:
Residents changing a birth certificate gender marker since 23 October 2014 file a Birth Certificate Request Form with an affidavit from a physician, certified nurse practitioner or physician's assistant confirming transgender status; the earlier sex reassignment surgery requirement no longer applies.

The Division of Motor Vehicles issues a corrected driver's licence on a Gender Designation Form signed by the applicant, without a medical affidavit.

An X gender option on driver's licences and birth certificates was announced in August 2019 and available from July 2020.

A June 2018 law requires transgender people to be correctly recorded on death certificates, effective immediately.

The 1995 exemption allowing discrimination in owner-occupied housing with three or fewer occupants was repealed with effect from 1 January 2023, and June 2023 legislation added explicit bans on discrimination in patient care, nursing and related healthcare.

Conversion therapy on minors and state funding for such practices were prohibited by a law signed on 19 July 2017 and effective immediately, after House votes of 69-0 and 62-0 and a Senate vote of 29-0.

In March 2025 the Rhode Island Interscholastic League replaced its policy of allowing participation consistent with gender identity with one that keeps transgender athletes eligible while making member schools responsible for compliance with all applicable state and federal law on gender-based eligibility.

Hate-crime penalty enhancements for crimes motivated by actual or perceived gender identity or expression, and the repeal of the gay and trans panic defence in June 2018, apply to residents as victims and as defendants.
outOfScopeNotes:
Passports, visas, entry screening and national enforcement are governed by national rules and are carried by the national record rather than here.

The July 2026 tier is a rights organisation's assessment, not a legal instrument, and creates no protection of its own.

The inventory does not set out which out-of-state actions the 2023 and 2024 shield provisions reach, how they have been invoked, or whether they have been tested in court.

No Rhode Island-specific hate-crime prosecution figures, enforcement incidents or trans-specific violence data appear in the sources reviewed.

The sources reviewed record no Rhode Island law restricting transgender people's use of sex-segregated facilities; the only facilities provision identified is the gender-neutral single-occupancy rule. Whether any municipal ordinances differ is not sourced.

The practical effect of the March 2025 interscholastic policy depends on how member schools apply national law, and no school-level decisions are documented in the inventory.

Whether the X option on driver's licences and birth certificates remains available after the 2019 announcement and July 2020 introduction is not addressed in the sources reviewed.
